title: Comment Explains Magic Numbers Without Rationale
pattern: A comment that merely restates the magic numbers present in the formula below it without explaining what they represent.
why_bad: Fails to explain intent. The comment leaves the reader asking 'Why width + 1?', 'Why multiply by 3?', and 'Why 200?'. It fails its primary job of explaining code that does not explain itself.
detection: Comments placed immediately above math formulas with hardcoded literals, where the comment restates the numbers without mapping them to clear domain concepts.
counterexample: A comment mapping each literal to a domain concept ('RGB pixels, +1 filter byte per row, fixed 200-byte PNG header'), with the literals extracted to named constants.
fix: Extract numbers to named constants and write a comment explaining the architectural reason behind the sizing values.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Inobvious Connection").
